title: Neonatal procedure calculators and procedure-guide provenance
_comment: calcs[]: { id, name, inputs[{var,label,unit}], formula{ text, machine }, src, quote, also?{src,quote}, applies?, notes[{text,src,quote}] }. machine types: 'linear' = const + sum(coef*var) with coef default 1 and 'neg': true meaning subtract that term, then 'then'[] ops applied in order (add|sub|mul|div by v); 'table' = rows[] each with its own when/src/quote; 'measure' = the measured value is the answer; 'nomogram' with values null = not computable; 'exchange' = multiplier x wt_kg x blood_volume_ml_per_kg[when]. No coefficient is pre-simplified (e.g. Shukla UVC is stored as (3 x BW + 9) / 2 + 1, not re-derived). guides{}: the quote behind every numbered sentence in kb/clinical-protocols/neonatal-*.json procedure guides.

calcs.name: UAC insertion length (Shukla and Ferrara, birth weight)

formula.text: UAC length (cm) = 3 x birth weight (kg) + 9

calcs.quote: To calculate the depth for inserting a UAC, we multiplied the neonate's weight in kilograms by 3 and added 9 cm.

notes.text: Add the umbilical stump length to the calculated length.
notes.quote: The umbilical stump length should be added to the calculation.

notes.text: Confirm the tip position on X-ray (or ultrasound) whatever method was used to estimate the length.
notes.quote: Umbilical catheter tip position should be confirmed radiologically after insertion, regardless of the method used to estimate placement length.

notes.text: UAC high position (recommended): descending thoracic aorta at T7 to T9. Low position: L3 to L5.
notes.quote: In high-position UAC, the tip is located in the descending thoracic aorta above the diaphragm at the level of the seventh to ninth thoracic vertebrae (T7 to T9), avoiding the origins of the mesenteric, celiac, and renal arteries. The tip of low-position UAC is located in the abdominal aorta at the level of the third to fifth lumber vertebrae (L3 to L5)

notes.text: In a Leiden before and after study the Shukla method placed UACs correctly first time more often than the Dunn method (87% vs 63%).
notes.quote: UACs in the Dunn-group were placed directly in the correct position in 63% (24/38) compared to the 87% (39/45) of cases in Shukla-group.

calcs.name: UVC insertion length (Shukla and Ferrara, birth weight)

formula.text: UVC length (cm) = (3 x birth weight (kg) + 9) / 2 + 1, that is, the Shukla UAC length halved plus 1 cm

calcs.quote: To calculate the depth for inserting a UAC, we multiplied the neonate's weight in kilograms by 3 and added 9 cm. To calculate the depth for inserting a UVC we used the insertion length of the UAC, divided this number by 2, and added 1 cm

notes.text: Add the umbilical stump length to the calculated length.
notes.quote: The umbilical stump length should be added to the calculation.

notes.text: Confirm the tip position on X-ray (or ultrasound) whatever method was used to estimate the length.
notes.quote: Umbilical catheter tip position should be confirmed radiologically after insertion, regardless of the method used to estimate placement length.

notes.text: UVC tip target: T8 to T9 (acceptable T7 to T10); high if above the body of T8, low if below the body of T9. Aim for the IVC and right atrium junction.
notes.quote: The optimal position of the UVC tip is at the junction between the inferior vena cava and right atrium, or at least well into the ductus venosus [ 19 ]. The ideal UVC tip position is at the level of T8-T9, but it could be anywhere between T7 and T10, high if above the body of T8 and low if below the body of T9

notes.text: The Shukla formula is frequently associated with over-insertion of the UVC.
notes.quote: As the Shukla formula is frequently associated with over-insertion of UVC, a revised formula has been proposed by Verheij et al.

notes.text: In the Leiden study 75% of Shukla-placed UVCs were too high, against 57% with Dunn.
notes.quote: The position of the catheter-tip of UVCs in the Dunn-group and the Shukla-group was too high in 57% (39/69) and 75% (63/84) of neonates, respectively.

also.quote: Verheij et al.'s formula (2013) | UVC length (cm) = [3 × BW (kg) + 9]/2

notes.quote: The revised formula is associated with less over-insertion of UVC without being complicated with a low-position UVC

notes.text: Low tips were more frequent with this weight formula than with the Gupta umbilicus-nipple method (32.9% vs 14.8%).
notes.quote: The modified Shukla group had a significantly abnormal catheter low tip position (n=23, 32.9%) compared to the Gupta group (n=13, 14.8%; p=0.02).

notes.quote: The Gupta method demonstrated a significantly higher rate of correct catheter placements (n=55, 62.5%) compared to the modified Shukla method (n=32, 45.7%; p=0.02).

calcs.name: ETT depth at lip by weight (weight + 6 cm; AAP/AHA, Tochen)

notes.text: Tochen's weight method adds 6 cm to birth weight for oral intubation.
notes.quote: In the weight-based method, so-called Tochen’s formula, the ETT insertion depth in oral intubation is obtained by adding 6 cm to the infant’s birth weight.

notes.text: Overestimation in extremely preterm infants.
notes.quote: This method often overestimates the insertion depth in extremely preterm infants less than 28 weeks of gestational age.

notes.text: ERC 2021: formulae may be unreliable for tracheal tube length; gestation-based lengths from observational data are shown in its Table 1.

calcs.name: ETT depth at lip by weight (7-8-9 rule)

formula.text: 7 cm at 1 kg, 8 cm at 2 kg, 9 cm at 3 kg; beyond 7 cm add 1 cm per additional kg

8 cm for infants weighing 2 kg
9 cm for infants weighing 3 kg.

notes.text: Overestimates tube length below 1500 g or above 2500 g.
notes.quote: The 7-8-9 rule has been found to be associated with an overestimation of tubal length if the infant weight is less than 1500 grams or more than 2500 grams

calcs.name: PICC insertion length, upper limb (surface measurement)

formula.text: Measure from the insertion site along the course of the vein to the head of the right clavicle, then down to the right third intercostal space just right of the sternum.

calcs.quote: The length of PICC to be placed through the upper body insertion is determined by measuring the distance from the insertion site through the course of the used vein to the head of the clavicle on the right side and down to the right third intercostal space just to the right of the sternum.

notes.text: Upper limb tip target: SVC at T3 to T5.
notes.quote: The optimal tip position of a PICC inserted through the upper limb veins is in the superior vena cava (SVC) at T3-T5 level.

notes.text: Variant (Wu 2022): arm abducted 90 degrees, measure from the puncture point through the right sternoclavicular joint down to the second intercostal space. Head or neck insertion: measure along the vein to the right nipple with the head turned to one side.
notes.quote: infants with a catheter inserted in the upper extremity had the length measured from the punctured point through the right sternoclavicular joint down to the second intercostal space with a 90° abduction of the upper extremity

notes.text: Variant (He 2024): for the upper limb measure from the elbow crease to the right sternoclavicular joint; for the cephalic vein measure to the third rib.
notes.quote: For the upper limb, the transverse line of the elbow to the right sternoclavicular joint was measured. The cephalic vein was measured from the pre-puncture point to the third rib.

notes.text: Surface measurement is imprecise: its tip-to-atrium distance fluctuated far more than ultrasound (range 1.5 cm vs 0.2 cm).
notes.quote: We noted that US measurements were considerably more stable than those of IVM, with a lesser fluctuation range (0.2 cm vs. 1.5 cm, p < 0.001)

notes.text: Keep the tip out of the heart: about 1 cm outside the cardiac silhouette in preterm and 2 cm in term infants.
notes.quote: Most studies have shown that the catheter tip should be positioned within the vena cava and outside the cardiac silhouette, that is, at approximately 1 cm beyond the cardiac silhouette for premature infants and 2 cm beyond for full-term infants.

calcs.name: PICC insertion length, lower limb (surface measurement)

formula.text: Measure from the insertion site along the course of the vein to the level of the xiphoid process (via groin and umbilicus).

calcs.quote: For PICC placed through lower limb insertion, the required insertion length is equal to the distance measured from the insertion site through the course of the used vein till the level of the xiphoid process

notes.text: Lower limb tip target: IVC between the diaphragm and right atrium at T8 to T10.
notes.quote: For lower limb-inserted PICC, the ideal tip position is in the inferior vena cava (IVC) between the diaphragm and the right atrium at T8-T10 level

notes.text: Variant (Fu 2025): abduct the leg 45 degrees and measure along the vein to the groin, umbilicus and xiphoid.
notes.quote: Prior to catheter placement, the infant's lower extremity was abducted at an angle of 45 degrees. The length of the catheter was then measured from the site of placement along the vein to the groin, umbilicus, and xiphoid process.

notes.text: Variant (Wu 2022): natural abduction, measure from the puncture point along the groin to the midpoint between umbilicus and xiphoid.

neonatal-intraosseous-access.text: Emergency route for drugs and fluids when umbilical venous or peripheral access fails. Use the flat anteromedial proximal tibia 1 to 2 cm below and 1 cm medial to the tibial tuberosity, stop at the loss of resistance, watch the limb for extravasation and remove the needle as soon as other access is secured.
neonatal-intraosseous-access.quote: The targeted penetration point of the proximal tibia is at its flat anteromedial surface, 1 to 2 cm below and 1 cm medial to the tibial tuberosity.

neonatal-intraosseous-access.text: Place an IO if venous access cannot be secured within three attempts and within 90 seconds.
neonatal-intraosseous-access.quote: It is recommended to be placed if venous access cannot be secured within three attempts and within 90 seconds

neonatal-intraosseous-access.text: Preferred site: proximal tibia, flat anteromedial surface 1 to 2 cm below and 1 cm medial to the tibial tuberosity. NRP 8th edition describes about 2 cm distal and 1 to 2 cm medial.

neonatal-intraosseous-access.text: Preferred site: proximal tibia, flat anteromedial surface 1 to 2 cm below and 1 cm medial to the tibial tuberosity. NRP 8th edition describes about 2 cm distal and 1 to 2 cm medial.

neonatal-intraosseous-access.text: If the tuberosity cannot be felt, use the flat medial tibia 1.5 to 2 cm distal to the patella.

neonatal-intraosseous-access.text: Second site: distal femur, anterior midline, 1 to 3 cm above the external condyles.
neonatal-intraosseous-access.quote: The distal femur penetration site is 1 to 3 cm above the external condyles in the anterior midline

neonatal-intraosseous-access.text: Keep clear of the growth plate: an ultrasound study aimed for at least 10 mm from it, and a puncture 10 mm below the tuberosity breached that margin in 53% of proximal sites. At 3000 to 4000 g the most suitable site was a median 13.0 mm below the tuberosity.

neonatal-lumbar-puncture.text: Sample CSF for suspected neonatal meningitis once the baby is stable. Sit the baby or lie it on its side with the spine flexed, enter below L2 to L3 (L3 to L4 or L4 to L5), use a 22 G or 25 G needle, advance in small steps checking for CSF, and fill 4 tubes with about 1 to 2 mL each.
neonatal-lumbar-puncture.quote: Since the lower end of the spinal cord in neonates is at the level of the body of the third lumber vertebra (L3), the LP must be performed below the L2-L3 interspace.

Confirm with bedside echo, remove or reposition the line, and if the heart is compressed drain by ultrasound-guided subxiphoid puncture with a 22G cannula aimed at the left shoulder, aspirating as you advance.

neonatal-exchange-transfusion.quote: The blood volume of newborns is usually about 80 mL·kg- 1

neonatal-exchange-transfusion.text: Measure serum bilirubin within 2 hours of the procedure.
neonatal-exchange-transfusion.quote: The STB level is measured within 2 hours of the procedure.

neonatal-exchange-transfusion.text: Check blood gas, glucose, electrolytes and calcium before and after; one series drew about 10 mL before and after for bilirubin, liver and renal function, gas, glucose and electrolytes.
neonatal-exchange-transfusion.quote: About 10 mL of blood was drawn from the arterial end before and after ex - change transfusion to detect indexes including bilirubin hepatic and renal functions, blood gas, blood glucose and electrolytes.

neonatal-exchange-transfusion.text: Mortality risk is about 1% in otherwise healthy and 12% in ill babies.
neonatal-exchange-transfusion.quote: mortality risk (1% in healthy babies, 12% in ill babies)
